![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095617/assets/4e203017dcac794ea45e70bfdd3203cada3d9766cd87d67f522fb88399e4be1f.png)

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves ${y}^{2}=2x$ and $y=x$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{2}{3},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type II region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\le x\le y},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095617/assets/a34ed2c8c25aa5c3c1e28e4458e11779f6b5948acbebdcb6e05b5bf1257689d4.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{3M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{y}\frac{3M}{2}|y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{2}/2}^{y}(y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}[x]_{x={y}^{2}/2}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y-2)^{2}(y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-{y}^{4}+6{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}+8y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}{[-\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}+\frac{3{y}^{4}}{2}-4{y}^{3}+4{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3M}{4}(-\frac{32}{5}+24-32+16-0) \\  & =\frac{6M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
